key_insight: HSImul3R closes the perception–simulation gap by integrating physics directly into the 3D reconstruction loop, producing human–scene interaction outputs that are both visually accurate and stable in physics engines.
problem_solved: Existing HSI reconstruction methods produce visually plausible results that often violate physical constraints, causing instability or failure when used in simulators and embodied AI tasks—HSImul3R makes casual captures (sparse views, monocular video) simulation-ready.
method: Physically-grounded bi-directional optimization: alternate perception updates with physics-based corrections to enforce contact, collision, and dynamic consistency.
Unified pipeline for casual captures: jointly optimize human pose, scene geometry, contacts, and physical parameters from sparse-view images or monocular video.
Physics-in-the-loop validation: run candidate reconstructions in a physics engine during optimization to reject/adjust physically implausible solutions.
impact: Enables reliable, simulator-ready HSI reconstructions from everyday captures, improving downstream tasks in robotics, virtual agents, and AR/VR by ensuring interactions are physically valid and stable.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing bi-directional loop between perception module and physics engine (optimize ↔ simulate ↔ correct).
Before/after comparison: visually plausible reconstruction that fails in simulation vs. HSImul3R output that remains stable under physics.
Contact and constraint visualization: heatmap or markers for contact points, normals, and applied forces during optimization.
Metric chart: simulation stability (e.g., contact violation, collapse rate) and reconstruction fidelity across sparse-view and monocular inputs.
paper_title: HSImul3R: Physics-in-the-Loop Reconstruction of Simulation-Ready Human-Scene Interactions
paper_authors: Yukang Cao, Haozhe Xie, Fangzhou Hong, Long Zhuo, Zhaoxi Chen
